title: "Studyflow: an executable visual notation for designing, running, and reporting experimental studies"

abstract: |
  Experimental studies in cognitive sciences are hard to replicate, verify, and understand. One cause of these difficulties is that a study's processes are scattered across protocols, code, data, and figures that are neither machine-readable nor mutually consistent. To bring these processes together, we present *Studyflow*. It is a visual notation that describes an entire study, in the vocabulary of experimental design, as one diagram humans can understand and computers can execute. Built on BPMN, an established process-modeling standard, the diagram is at once the study's protocol, runnable implementation, data model, analysis plan, provenance record, and publication figure. The documents a study requires, such as the participant flow and checklists, are generated from the Studyflow diagram, ensuring consistency across documents by design. Studyflow tracks every change to a study and records what happened and when. A study can be validated and simulated before data collection, rerun from the same file, and compared with its registered version to expose any deviation. We demonstrate Studyflow on a complete study with artificial agents and release open source tools to create, validate, and run diagrams. Studyflow thus lays the foundation for a new generation of research tools that make studies transparent, verifiable, and replicable for human and AI stakeholders alike.
impact-statement: |
  A single human-understandable, machine-readable diagram serves as a study's protocol, experiment orchestration script, data model, analysis plan, data provenance, and publication figure.
keywords:
  - scientific workflows
